To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
five new polymorphisms, four of them tightly linked to the hereditary hemochromaticosis (HFE), have been detected in the 6p21 HLA region.
five new polymorphisms were detected in a region of 700-kb, four of which are linked to the hemochromatotic locus and may represent starting points for its identification.
the HFE region contains a high density of polymorphic markers, and that a genomic contig spanning the entire region is now available.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of polymorphic markers in the HFE region of the human genome, and the development of PCR protocols to be applied to these markers.
the identification of polymorphic markers and with the characterization of the gene content of a 700-kbp region of band 6, which contains the HFE gene.
the identification of polymorphic markers in the HFE gene region, with a view to the identification of the HFE locus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, despite a large number of markers, the HFE gene is still not isolated.
, in addition to the HLA class-I region, the HFE region contains at least five other genes, which are expressed and which are linked to the HLA region.
the HFE gene lies within the 225 B1 insert.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we now have 10 markers, 6 polymorphic and 4 not, that can be used in a PCR-based assay to detect the HFE locus in a large number of families.
we have identified five new markers, four of which are tightly linked to HFE, in the 225 B1 yeast artificial chromosome, which covers approximately 700 kb of DNA.
we have been able to identify 11 new polymorphic DNA markers and 15 expressed sequences in a 700-kB region of the HLA class-I region, 5 of which have been found to be polymorphic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of the use of a yeast artificial chromosome insert and the use of PCR protocols is a powerful tool for the isolation of new polymorphisms and for the generation of markers useful for the study of a complex genetic trait.
the HFE gene could be isolated by using the PCR-based approach described in this report.

the use of PCR-based strategies in the analysis of genomic regions of high gene content may be useful in the identification of polymorphic markers linked to disease loci and in the isolation of expressed sequences.
